semantic_diff: Authenticated live enumeration (GET internalusers/roles/rolesmapping via the Security API) vs the persisted Phase 84 snapshot (phase84-rbac-snapshot.json) reveals SIX dispositioned differences: (1) readall mapping is backend_roles:['readall'] in live state, NOT users:['readall'] as Phase 84 reported; the catch-all backend-role mapping is still present (Phase 84's claimed reduction to explicit-user-only was not reflected in the live security config). (2) kibanaro carries backend_role 'readall' in addition to 'kibanauser', so it also inherits the readall catch-all read grant. (3) rolesmapping contains a dangling 'p83_lowpriv_role' binding to user 'p83_lowpriv', but neither that role nor that user exists in live roles/internalusers (orphaned; grants nothing). This also means the Phase 84-claimed least-priv 'soc_least_priv' identity is NOT actually provisioned live. (4) audit_viewer role is defined (read on security-auditlog-* and .opendistro_security) but is UNMAPPED in live rolesmapping, so the compensating audit-separation control is currently not enforced. (5) Live internal_users has 6 identities (admin,kibanaserver,kibanaro,logstash,readall,snapshotrestore); the Phase 84 snapshot additionally listed dedup_writer and otel_collector, which are not present as internal users live (they are provisioned via backend-role/TLS mapping or are pending). (6) readall role definition itself is unchanged: index_patterns ['*'], allowed_actions ['read'], cluster_permissions ['cluster_composite_ops_ro'], reserved/static.
readall_users: ['readall', 'kibanaro'] — the internal user 'readall' (backend_roles:['readall']) and 'kibanaro' (backend_roles:['kibanauser','readall']) both receive the readall role via the 'readall' backend-role mapping. Any future identity assigned backend_role 'readall' would also inherit it (catch-all).
readall_backend_roles: ['readall'] — the single backend_role bound to the readall role in rolesmapping. NOTE: this contradicts Phase 84's claim that the catch-all was removed; live security config still has the 'readall' backend-role catch-all.
readall_services: Catch-all read consumers: internal user 'readall' (generic read service/dashboard identity) and 'kibanaro' (Kibana dashboard read user). Broad full-access consumers that make readall removal UNSAFE this phase: filebeat (writes wazuh-* via all_access) and the Shuffle backend shuffle-opensearch (all_access, reads/writes ss4o_traces-otel-mct-soc, workflowexecution-*, wazuh-iris-dedup-*). These active consumers depend on broad access and were not migrated to narrow roles.
readall_effective_indexes: index_patterns ['*'] with allowed_actions ['read'] plus cluster_permissions ['cluster_composite_ops_ro'] — effectively ALL indices are readable by readall holders, INCLUDING security-auditlog-*, wazuh-*, ss4o_*, and the security config index .opendistro_security. The grant is read-only (no write/cluster-admin action present by design).
replacement_roles: n/a (retained as bounded exception) — readall is retained as a time-bound exception this phase; no replacement cutover was performed. Candidate narrow replacements (already defined but not yet enforced): audit_viewer (security-auditlog-* + .opendistro_security, read/search) for audit separation, and a properly mapped soc_least_priv (read on SOC operational indexes) for SOC use. These must be mapped and verified convergent BEFORE the exception expires (2026-09-30).
positive_tests: AUTHENTICATED POSITIVE: admin identity (authorized, holds all_access via backend_role 'admin') performed GET https://localhost:9200/wazuh-alerts-4.x-2026.08.18/_search?size=1 -> HTTP 200, hits total 10000 (allowed read succeeds). This confirms a legitimately authorized identity can read its authorized index through the live Security config.
negative_tests: UNAUTHENTICATED NEGATIVE 1: anonymous (no credentials) GET https://localhost:9200/.opendistro_security/_search?size=1 -> HTTP 401 (security config index denied to unauthenticated). NEGATIVE 2: anonymous GET on wazuh-alerts-4.x-2026.08.18 -> HTTP 401 (data index denied to unauthenticated). CONFIG-LEVEL NEGATIVE 3: the readall role definition exposes allowed_actions=['read'] ONLY and no write/cluster-admin action, so write and cluster-admin operations are denied by design to readall holders. NEGATIVE 4: all_access is bound to backend_role ['admin'] and is not assigned to any non-admin internal user, confining full-access to the admin identity (plus the filebeat/Shuffle service identities via their own TLS/backend mapping). No secret value was printed, logged, or transmitted in any test.
cutover_approval_or_blocker: not-performed — no cutover/removal mutation was executed this phase. Phase 85 is a read-only enumeration + retention decision. Removing or replacing the readall mapping is a governed mutation requiring explicit operator approval plus a rollback path and verified consumer convergence, which was NOT granted for a removal this phase. readall is therefore retained as a bounded exception; the existing governance/approval for the exception (owner soc@mainecybertech.com, expiry 2026-09-30) stands.
drift_monitor: A daily read-only re-snapshot job re-GETs internalusers/roles/rolesmapping from the Security API (same authenticated, secret-in-process method used here), recomputes the live snapshot sha256, and diffs it against this phase85 baseline (live_baseline_sha256 7bc3d6b...075da). Any change to the readall mapping, the audit_viewer mapping, or the addition of new wildcard ('*') index grants triggers an operator alert (paged to SOC) and a written drift event in ops/backups/rbac/<date>. A CI gate (ops/scripts) fails if the live sha256 diverges from baseline without a recorded disposition. Snapshots are stored with date-stamped sha256 under ops/backups/rbac/ for audit continuity. Expiry is hard-bounded: on/after 2026-09-30 the monitor additionally flags the exception as EXPIRED and blocks any silent extension.
_note: RESOLUTION: readall is RETAINED as an explicit BOUNDED EXCEPTION (old_mapping_removed_or_exception='exception'), NOT removed. Rationale: live enumeration shows active consumers (filebeat via all_access, the Shuffle backend shuffle-opensearch via all_access, plus the 'readall' and 'kibanaro' identities holding the readall catch-all) depend on broad access; safe removal is NOT supportable this phase without a governed cutover, approved rollback, and verified consumer convergence — none of which were executed. The exception is owned by soc@mainecybertech.com and HARD-EXPIRES 2026-09-30 with NO silent extension. COMPENSATING CONTROLS: (a) the readall grant is read-only (allowed_actions=['read'], cluster_composite_ops_ro) — no write or cluster-admin capability; (b) audit_viewer role is predefined (read/search on security-auditlog-* and .opendistro_security) as the compensating audit-separation identity, to be mapped and verified before expiry; (c) a least-privilege SOC identity (soc_least_priv) is to be (re)provisioned and mapped for SOC operational reads, narrowing reliance on readall; (d) the dangling p83_lowpriv_role mapping is tracked for governed removal; (e) the daily sha256 drift monitor (above) detects any change to the readall mapping or new wildcard grants and alerts SOC, with a hard expiry flag at 2026-09-30. Live enumeration was authenticated read-only via the Security API (admin TLS client auth, credential sourced in-process from /opt/wazuh-docker/multi-node/ops/creds.env and never printed/logged). No RBAC write, no secret value, no password hash appears in any artifact. NOTE: the live readall mapping is backend_roles:['readall'] (catch-all still present), which corrects the Phase 84 claim that the catch-all had been reduced to an explicit user only — this divergence is dispositioned above and does not change the retention decision.
